title: [Feature][2/N] Add GLM KDA RecoverSSM framework integration
body:
### What this PR does / why we need it?

Add the GLM KDA RecoverSSM framework integration for Ascend Model Runner V2, split from #19133 as part 2/N. Connect the model's compact record caches, upstream request/commit metadata, NPU graph staging and post-sampling commit lifecycle. Adapt Mooncake pull PD transfer and account for the GLM cache pools.

The existing `--use-replayssm` option selects the GLM path after validating speculative decoding, Mamba cache mode `none`, disabled prefix caching/stochastic rounding, PP/PCP/DCP=1 and supported Mooncake connectors. Other models and disabled configurations retain the upstream selection behavior.

This framework directly uses `kda_recoverssm_verify` and `KDARecoverSSMCommitContext` from [part 1/N, #20128](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/pull/20128), now merged into `main`. The operator implementation is inherited unchanged from the base branch. RecoverSSM eager/graph four-card E2E cases are enabled alongside the native path.

The context binding patch is limited to GLM workers with RecoverSSM enabled; remove it when upstream exposes a backend context factory. The configuration validator patch can be removed when upstream supports GLM KDA selection. Both removal plans are recorded in the patch registry.

The platform and worker KV dtype patches are kept identical to the base branch; the unrelated KV dtype registry and FP8 fallback compatibility changes have been removed.

### Does this PR introduce any user-facing change?

Enable GLM KDA RecoverSSM with the existing `--use-replayssm` option alongside speculative decoding. Requires Mamba cache mode `none`, prefix caching and stochastic rounding disabled, and PP/PCP/DCP=1. Supported PD connectors are `MooncakeConnectorV2` and `MooncakePullConnector`. Native AscendC remains the default with the option disabled.

### How was this patch tested?

End-to-end validation combines the RecoverSSM Triton operators (part 1/N, #20128) with this framework integration. The results below were recorded on the integrated implementation `97023fefd7106fff42b480e6ed629979b35d7d9e` after fully removing the unrelated KV dtype compatibility commit `d2e1c892b`, paired with vLLM `544f182d9f0c9bfe8bd7645525951d5e3692a542`.

Real-weight GSM8K accuracy check (2026-10-28): the same first 30 test questions for each condition, 4-shot, greedy generation, seed 1024, reasoning effort `low`, up to 8192 output tokens and 30 concurrent clients. Both devices use ordinary BF16 KV, MTP5 and target/draft `FULL_DECODE_ONLY` graphs. Weight quantization remains A3 W8A8 and A5 MXFP8. Maximum context is 16384, `max_num_seqs=12` and `max_num_batched_tokens=4096`.

| Configuration | Recover off correct / total | Recover on correct / total | Natural stops per condition |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| A3 W8A8, BF16 KV, DP8/TP2 | 29/30 | 28/30 | 30/30 |
| A5 MXFP8, BF16 KV, DP8/TP1 | 29/30 | 29/30 | 30/30 |

All four groups completed without output truncation. A3 has one additional incorrect answer with RecoverSSM enabled; A5 has the same correct count. Worker records confirm the RecoverSSM flag, BF16 KV and target/draft graph mode on all 16 A3 workers and all 8 A5 workers. An A5 startup attempt failed during HCCL initialization before requests; a retry with unchanged parameters completed the test.

This 30-question check covers startup and accuracy; it does not establish full-dataset accuracy equivalence or BF16 KV performance.

- vLLM main: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/commit/544f182d9f0c9bfe8bd7645525951d5e3692a542
